name: Cable Bicep Curl
machineIdentification: A cable pulley set at the lowest position with a straight or EZ bar attached. You stand facing the tower.
instructions: Set a pulley at the bottom and attach a straight bar.
Stand a step back, holding the bar with palms up.
Keep your elbows tucked at your sides.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
keyCues: Pin your elbows to your ribs the whole set.
Keep tension at the bottom — don't fully relax.
Squeeze the biceps at the top.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start each rep.
Letting the elbows drift forward at the top.
Rushing the lowering half.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows tucked at your sides.
Curl both dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
keyCues: Keep your upper arms still — only the forearms move.
Straighten fully at the bottom of every rep.
Take three seconds to lower.
commonMistakes: Rocking backward to swing the weights up.
Stopping short of full extension.
Letting the elbows travel forward at the top.

name: Preacher Curl Machine
machineIdentification: A seat with a large angled arm pad in front and handles at the far end. Your upper arms rest flat on the pad so they can't move.
instructions: Set the seat so your armpits sit near the top of the pad.
Rest your upper arms flat on the pad.
Take the handles with palms facing up.
Curl the handles up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
keyCues: Keep both upper arms glued to the pad.
Control the bottom — that's where biceps tear.
Don't let the stack rest between reps.
commonMistakes: Lifting the elbows off the pad to finish a rep.
Dropping fast into the stretched bottom position.
Setting the seat too low so the shoulders take over.

name: Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows tucked at your sides.
Curl the dumbbells up without rotating your wrists.
Lower slowly to full extension.
keyCues: Hold the neutral grip throughout — thumbs stay up.
Keep your upper arms still.
Alternate arms if it helps you stay strict.
commonMistakes: Rotating the wrists into a normal curl.
Using the shoulders to swing the weight.
Cutting off the bottom of the range.

name: Tricep Pushdown
machineIdentification: A cable pulley set high with a straight bar or rope attached. You stand facing the tower, close to the frame.
instructions: Set the pulley high and attach a bar or rope.
Stand close, gripping the attachment at chest height.
Tuck your elbows against your sides.
Push down until your arms are fully straight.
Let it rise back to chest height under control.
keyCues: Keep your elbows pinned — they shouldn't drift.
Straighten fully and squeeze at the bottom.
Lean forward slightly and keep the torso still.
commonMistakes: Using body weight to push the bar down.
Letting the elbows flare out and forward.
Stopping short of full lockout.

name: Overhead Cable Tricep Extension
machineIdentification: A cable pulley with a rope attached, set at head height or above. You face away from the tower with the rope behind your head.
instructions: Attach a rope and set the pulley at about head height.
Take the rope and turn to face away from the tower.
Step forward into a split stance, rope behind your head.
Extend your arms straight forward and up.
Let your hands travel back behind your head under control.
keyCues: Keep your elbows pointing forward and close together.
Get a full stretch behind the head each rep.
Brace your core so you don't arch your back.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows flare wide.
Arching the lower back to press the weight.
Standing too close and losing tension.

name: Dumbbell Overhead Tricep Extension
instructions: Hold one dumbbell with both hands, cupping the top end.
Press it overhead until your arms are straight.
Lower it behind your head by bending only the elbows.
Extend back to straight arms.
keyCues: Keep your elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Keep your ribs down so the back doesn't arch.
Lower until you feel a stretch, then press.
commonMistakes: Letting the elbows flare out to the sides.
Arching the lower back under heavier dumbbells.
Moving the shoulders instead of just the elbows.

name: Assisted Dip
machineIdentification: Usually the same frame as the assisted pull-up machine — two parallel bars at hip height with the padded knee platform below. More weight means more help.
instructions: Set the assistance weight and step onto the side rails.
Grip the parallel dip bars.
Kneel onto the padded platform.
Lower until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
keyCues: Keep your elbows tracking back, not flaring wide.
Lean forward slightly to involve the chest.
Stop lowering if you feel a pinch in the shoulder.
commonMistakes: Dropping too deep and straining the shoulder.
Bouncing out of the bottom position.
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears.
